subject: Request: SDK rolling support matrix & deprecation alignment
messages:
From: Mike Chen <mike@integratech.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Support: SDK support matrix & deprecation alignment

Hi Priya —

Hope you’re well. Quick note from Integratech: we’ve been notified by our platform team that Redwood is planning the next SDK deprecation wave in Q1. We rely on two legacy client versions (py-1.x and js-2.x) in a subset of our integrations and need to understand the exact support window so we can map internal rollout and procurement timelines.

Can you share: 1) the proposed deprecation date for those versions, 2) recommended migration paths and any compatibility shims Redwood can offer, and 3) expected SLA/perf differences between the legacy and new SDKs?

We’ve attached a brief usage extract (current active installs by region) to help prioritize. Integratech would like to align any breaking changes to avoid an emergency patch cycle in January.

Thanks —
Mike Chen
Head of Integrations, Integratech
attachments: Integratech_sdk_usage_Q3_2026.csv (csv, 42KB)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Chen <mike@integratech.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Support: SDK support matrix & deprecation alignment

Hi Mike —

Thanks for the heads up and for the usage extract. Looping in Marcus (alliances) and Vanessa (partner operations) so we can scope a partner-aligned timeline. A few quick asks from our side to make the proposal specific:

- Can you confirm approximate % of traffic and number of paying customers still on py-1.x and js-2.x (ballpark is fine).
- Any regulatory/contractual constraints (e.g., pinned versions in customer contracts) that would require an exception window?

High level: we typically publish a 90-day deprecation notice for minor SDKs and 180 days for major-breaking SDKs, but we can propose a partner-specific cadence if Integratech needs more runway. Marcus — can you draft a partner support matrix with options (90/180/270-day windows + a paid extended-support offer)?

I’ll turn this into a formal timeline doc once we have the numbers.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

From: Mike Chen <mike@integratech.com>

Subject: Re: Support: SDK support matrix & deprecation alignment

On Mon, Nov 23, 2026 at 9:02 AM Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Mike —
> 
> Thanks for the heads up and for the usage extract.

Hi Priya —

Thanks for the quick response. Attached is a small breakdown by customer tier and region. Quick summary: py-1.x accounts for ~14% of token volume (mostly EMEA & a few US enterprise customers) and js-2.x accounts for ~9% (commercial customers in US). We have two enterprise customers with contractual pinned versions (redactedsystems.com and bluepeak.ai) — they will need at least a 6-month runway or a negotiated change order.

We appreciate the flexibility on timing. Priority asks: 1) a written partner timeline we can share with our legal and procurement teams; 2) a fallback plan (compat shim or proxy) that buys us tokens-level compatibility for 60–90 days post-deprecation.

-Mike
attachments: Integratech_sdk_usage_Q3_2026_detailed.csv (csv, 128KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Mike Chen <mike@integratech.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:36:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Support: SDK support matrix & deprecation alignment

Hi all —

Thanks Mike for the usage breakdown, that’s helpful. Draft proposal below (partner-specific option set) — this is intended as a conversation starter, not final legal language:

Option A — Standard: 90-day notice for minor SDKs; 180-day for breaking changes. No extended support included.

Option B — Partner Extended (Integratech): 180-day notice for minor SDKs; 270-day for breaking changes + paid extended support (90 days post-deprecation) at a partner rate. Includes 2 engineer-days of migration consulting and priority triage for critical regressions.

Option C — Contractual Exception: 6-month pinned exceptions for named enterprise accounts (requires minimal contract amendment + SOW).

Compatibility shim: We can provide a lightweight, open-source proxy shim that maps legacy client calls to the new SDK surface for up to 90 days after deprecation. It would be community-maintained but Redwood will publish the repo and a basic support doc. For mission-critical enterprise customers, we can offer a managed support add-on (paid) for the shim.

Proposed next steps:
- Priya/Marcus: agree on the option to present to Integratech.
- Vanessa: if partner opts for Extended or Contractual Exception, we’ll prepare pricing and SOW template.
- Mike: share the two enterprise contract contacts so we can scope the exception SOWs.

Link: https://docs.redwood.ai/partner/sdks/support-matrix-v1 (draft)

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Head of Alliances | Redwood Inference

From: Mike Chen <mike@integratech.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Support: SDK support matrix & deprecation alignment

Marcus —

Appreciate the clear options. Integratech would like to request Option B (Partner Extended) for both py-1.x and js-2.x with the following asks:

- 270-day support for breaking changes, plus the paid 90-day extension for the shim for primary customers.
- The managed shim offering would be preferable for our two enterprise customers (they want an SLA on the shim itself).
- We’ll need a written timeline to show procurement and legal today; can you publish a partner timeline PDF by COB Friday?

If Redwood agrees, we are prepared to sign a short addendum that covers the extended-support fees.

Also looping in a short quoted question from our legal team about whether the shim would be covered under Redwood’s standard maintenance policies or require a separate SOW.

-Mike

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Chen <mike@integratech.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 14:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Support: SDK support matrix & deprecation alignment

Mike —

Thanks — we can proceed with Option B for Integratech. Summary of the agreed partner plan (for Integratech):

- Timeline: Redwood will publish a partner timeline PDF today (link below). Official deprecation notices will be sent per the chosen window but Integratech receives the Extended timeline: 270 days for breaking SDK changes.
- Shim: Redwood will publish the open-source compatibility shim and offer a managed-shim add-on (SLA-backed) as a paid SOW for named enterprise customers.
- Migration support: includes 2 engineer-days of migration consulting; additional days can be purchased via SOW.
- Pricing: Vanessa will circulate the partner-rate schedule and a short addendum template after this email.

Next steps (action owners):
- Vanessa: partner-rate spreadsheet + SOW template (ETA: EOD Monday).
- Marcus: publish partner timeline PDF and addendum draft (ETA: EOD Friday).
- Mike: share enterprise contact emails for contract exceptions and confirm acceptance of the partner terms.

We’ve attached the draft support matrix and timeline. Thanks for moving quickly on this — we’ll follow up with a DocuSign link if Integratech approves the addendum.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference
